q: In which month does the Eredivisie normally take its winter break?
note: Confirmed on the Eredivisie page, the winterstop falls in January.

q: A gold star on a Dutch professional club's shirt stands for how many national titles?
sub: The KNVB brought the champions' star in for professional clubs in 2007.
note: Duplicate. The shipping row 'Ajax's 2011 championship was their 30th. What did it earn the club on its shirt? A third star' is the same arithmetic fact mirrored. The fact itself is right, a star is ten titles, but it cannot ship twice.

q: The Eredivisie changed its relegation rules for 2019-20. How many clubs went down automatically from then on?
sub: The club finishing 16th still had to go into the play-offs.
note: Confirmed: from 2019-20 the bottom two go down automatically and the 16th club plays the play-offs.

q: Which Dutch referee took charge of the Euro 2020 final between Italy and England at Wembley?
sub: The first Dutchman to referee a European Championship final.
note: Confirmed: Italy against England at Wembley, 11 July 2021, and he was the first Dutchman to referee a European Championship final.

q: The world's first live video referee decision came in the Netherlands in 2016. Was it in the Eredivisie or the KNVB Cup?
note: Confirmed: the first live video decision came in the KNVB Cup tie Ajax against Willem II on 21 September 2016.

q: Which Dutch club did the goalkeeper Hans van Breukelen win six league titles and the 1988 European Cup with?
note: Confirmed: six titles with PSV in 1985-86, 86-87, 87-88, 88-89, 90-91 and 91-92, plus the 1988 European Cup, where he saved Veloso's penalty.

q: A crowd of 65,150 watched an Eredivisie match in 1969-70, the biggest the league had seen. Which two clubs were playing?
note: Was phrased as a live record, 'The record Eredivisie crowd'. Anchored to the closed season. Figure confirmed: 65,150 for Feyenoord against Ajax in 1969-70.

q: Which club led the Eredivisie table from the first round to the last in 2016-17?
note: Confirmed on the records list: Ajax in 1997-98 and Feyenoord in 2016-17 led from round one to round 34, so the season anchor keeps the answer unique.

q: What is the Dutch name for the play-offs held after the regular Eredivisie season?
note: Confirmed.

q: Which club won 30 of its 34 matches in 1971-72, losing only once?
sub: They also conceded just 20 goals all season.
note: Confirmed on the season page: 30 wins, 3 draws, 1 defeat, 104 for and 20 against.

q: Which club did the goalkeeper Jan van Beveren defend for right through the 1970s?
note: Duplicate. Shipping already tells the table that Jan van Beveren was PSV's goalkeeper, in 'Which PSV goalkeeper quit the national team in 1975 with Willy van der Kuijlen'. This asks exactly that.

q: From which season was the video assistant referee used in every Eredivisie match?
note: Confirmed: VAR in every Eredivisie match from 2018-19.

q: Which Dutch club did the goalkeeper Ed de Goey leave to join Chelsea in 1997?
note: Confirmed: Feyenoord from 1990 to 1997, then Chelsea.

q: Björn Kuipers refereed the 2014 final between Real Madrid and Atlético Madrid. Which competition was it?
note: Duplicate by spoiler, and close to self-answering. The surviving extreme row names 'the 2014 Champions League final' outright. Fact confirmed on nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bjorn_Kuipers.

q: How many league matches does each Eredivisie club play in a normal season?
note: Confirmed: eighteen clubs, 34 matches.

q: Which club scored 112 league goals in 1997-98?
sub: They conceded just 22 goals in the same season.
note: Fact confirmed on the 1997-98 season page, 112 scored. Rewrote the sub, which handed the table the answers to two other rows in this slice, the 89 points and the plus 90.

q: Which club was Luis Suárez playing for when he scored 35 Eredivisie goals in 2009-10?
note: Confirmed: 35 goals for Ajax in 2009-10, the season's golden boot.

q: Feyenoord and Ajax once produced a 9-5, the highest scoring match in Eredivisie history. Which of the two won it?
note: Duplicate. Straight mirror of the normal row 'Which club did Feyenoord beat 9-5 in 1960-61', same match from the other side, plus it is a coin flip and phrased as a live record. Kept the anchored normal one.

q: Which club had André Onana in goal when he was voted the least beaten keeper of both 2016-17 and 2017-18?
note: Confirmed on the Van Leeuwen trophy list, Onana won it for 2016-17 and 2017-18 with Ajax.

q: In which month does an Eredivisie season normally finish?
note: Confirmed, the season usually ends in May.

q: Vincent Janssen was Eredivisie top scorer in 2015-16 with 27 goals. Which club was he playing for?
note: Confirmed: 27 goals for AZ in 2015-16.

q: Ajax won 5-0 in the KNVB Cup in September 2016 in the first match anywhere with a live video referee. Who were the opponents?
note: Confirmed: Ajax 5-0 Willem II in the cup on 21 September 2016, the first match anywhere with a live video referee. Kept in preference to the extreme Kali row, which named Willem II and gave this away.

q: Which Dutch club did the goalkeeper Michel Vorm leave for Swansea City in 2011?
note: Confirmed: FC Utrecht to Swansea City in 2011, straight after his first match of 2011-12.

q: Which club did the goalkeeper Kenneth Vermeer join from Ajax in the summer of 2014?
sub: Ajax felt tricked into selling him cheaply to a direct rival.
note: Confirmed: August 2014, and the agent dealing behind Ajax's back is exactly why Overmars changed policy on selling to rivals.

q: Which Dutch club did the goalkeeper Jasper Cillessen join Ajax from in 2011?
note: Confirmed: NEC to Ajax, 27 August 2011.

q: Which referee handed out thirteen yellow cards in ADO Den Haag against Feyenoord in August 2014?
sub: No Eredivisie match had brought more.
note: Confirmed on the records list: 'ADO Den Haag - Feyenoord, 10-8-2014, scheidsrechter Danny Makkelie', thirteen yellows. The sub was a present-tense record, now past.

q: Which club won 22 league matches in a row between May and December 1987?
note: Confirmed: 22 in a row between May and December 1987.

q: Which club did Feyenoord beat 9-5 in 1960-61 on the way to their first Eredivisie title?
note: Confirmed: Feyenoord 9-5 Ajax in 1960-61, their first Eredivisie title, 100 goals scored.

q: Which Dutch referee took charge of the 2013 Europa League final between Chelsea and Benfica in Amsterdam?
note: Confirmed: Chelsea against Benfica at the Amsterdam ArenA, 15 May 2013.

q: Which Dutch coach had won the Eredivisie six times by the end of 2017-18, more than any other?
note: Confirmed: six titles with PSV, more than any other coach in the Dutch league, and the question is properly anchored to 2017-18.

q: A video referee ruled out a late Stijn Wuytens header in the 2017 KNVB Cup semi-final. Which club did he play for?
sub: The video referee spotted a push by his team-mate Levi Garcia.
note: Confirmed on nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Videoscheidsrechter: Higler as video referee ruled Wuytens' goal out for a push by Levi Garcia. The old sub claimed AZ won on penalties, which I could not confirm, so the sourced detail replaces it.

q: Which club did Heerenveen beat 9-0 in October 2007?
note: Duplicate. Three surviving rows name 'Heerenveen's 9-0 win over Heracles Almelo in October 2007' in the question, so the opponents are given away. Match verified as 7 October 2007.

q: Between 2006 and 2019, how many Eredivisie clubs went down automatically each season?
sub: The clubs finishing 16th and 17th went into the play-offs.
note: Confirmed: from 2006 to 2019 only the bottom club went down automatically, with 16th and 17th into the play-offs.

q: Which club did Heinz Stuy keep three straight European Cup final clean sheets for?
note: Correct: Ajax, and he is the only keeper to keep three straight European Cup final clean sheets, 1971 to 1973. Pulled from normal to easy, three European Cups in a row is Ajax to anyone who has watched Dutch football, and the deck is light on easy.

q: Which club's defence went 1159 minutes without conceding across 2004-05, setting an Eredivisie record?
sub: Two keepers shared the run, Heurelho Gomes and Edwin Zoetebier.
note: 1159 minutes across 2004-05 confirmed, with Zoetebier and Gomes sharing the run. Reworded so the record is set at a closed moment rather than standing.

q: Before the 1995-96 season, how many points did an Eredivisie club get for a win?
note: Duplicate. Exact mirror of the shipping row 'In which season did the Eredivisie switch to three points for a win? 1995-96'.

q: Which Feyenoord striker scored in the 99th minute against FC Utrecht in November 2016, the latest goal the league had seen?
note: Confirmed: 27 November 2016, FC Utrecht 3-3 Feyenoord, nine minutes added after Robbin Ruiter's injury. 'The latest goal in Eredivisie history' was a live record, now put in the past.

q: Which 17-year-old scored a hat-trick for PSV against NEC in August 2013?
sub: He was 17 years and 196 days old, the youngest to do it at the time.
note: Confirmed: 10 August 2013, PSV 5-0 NEC, 17 years and 196 days. Took the live 'youngest in Eredivisie history' out of the question and put the age in the sub.

q: Which Dutch club did the goalkeeper Hans van Breukelen play for before Nottingham Forest?
note: Confirmed: FC Utrecht from 1976 to 1982, then Nottingham Forest.

q: Which Deventer club did the goalkeeper Jan Jongbloed finish his career at, playing past his 44th birthday?
sub: The oldest player ever to appear in the Eredivisie.
note: Duplicate. Mirror of the surviving ball row about Jongbloed still playing for Go Ahead Eagles at 44. Record confirmed: 44 years, 9 months and 14 days, in 1985.

q: Which club scored 100 league goals on the way to the 1960-61 Eredivisie title?
note: Duplicate. The shipping row 'Which Czech coached Feyenoord to the 1960-61 title, their first of the Eredivisie era' already states that Feyenoord won 1960-61, which is the whole answer here. The 100 goals check out on the season page.

q: Which Rotterdam club did the goalkeeper Eddy Treijtel play for in the early 1970s?
note: Duplicate. The surviving ball row calls him 'the Feyenoord goalkeeper Eddy Treijtel', so the answer is printed on another card. Feyenoord 1968-1979 confirmed.

q: Which two clubs drew 6-6 in the Eredivisie in 1990-91?
sub: No Eredivisie draw had produced more goals.
note: Season confirmed as 1990-91 on the season page, the 6-6 sits in the RKC row against FC Twente. Moved the live 'highest scoring draw in Eredivisie history' out of the question into an anchored sub.

q: Which Amsterdam club did the goalkeeper Piet Schrijvers join from FC Twente in 1974?
note: Correct: Twente to Ajax in July 1974. Pulled from normal to easy, since 'Which Amsterdam club' in 1974 leaves only one answer and the deck needs easy rows.

q: Which club was Klaas-Jan Huntelaar at when he started the 2005-06 season, before joining Ajax in January and taking the golden boot?
note: Confirmed: Heerenveen for the first half of 2005-06, Ajax from January, 33 goals in all.

q: Which Brazilian was Eredivisie top scorer in 2006-07 with 34 goals for Heerenveen?
note: Confirmed: 34 goals in 31 matches for Heerenveen in 2006-07.

q: Which club was on the wrong end of the fastest red card in Eredivisie history when a PSV player went after 29 seconds?
note: Duplicate. Mirror of the hard row 'Which PSV defender was sent off after 29 seconds at NAC Breda in 2014-15'. Same 29-second incident from the other end.

q: Which Enschede club lost only three of 34 matches in 1971-72 but drew fourteen of them?
sub: They finished third, fifteen points behind Ajax.
note: Record confirmed: 17 wins, 14 draws, 3 defeats, third on 48 points against Ajax's 63. The sub claimed the meanest defence in Eredivisie history, a standing record, and it also gave away the surviving 13-goals row.

q: In which season did the Eredivisie settle on eighteen clubs, the size it kept from then on?
note: Duplicate. The shipping row 'For four seasons from 1962-63 the Eredivisie was cut from eighteen clubs to how many' hands you 1966-67 by arithmetic. 'The size it kept from then on' is also a standing claim.

q: Which Ajax forward scored six goals in one Eredivisie match, an 8-1 win over AZ '67 in 1970-71?
sub: It happened on 29 November 1970.
note: He scored six, on 29 November 1970. Ajax's own account calls it a double hat-trick but Cruyff himself rejected that reading, so 'two hat-tricks' is arguable where 'six goals' is not.

q: Which club conceded only 13 goals in 1971-72, the fewest in an Eredivisie season up to 2017-18?
sub: Their keeper Piet Schrijvers won the least beaten goalkeeper trophy for it.
note: Confirmed: 13 conceded in 1971-72, and Schrijvers did win the Tonny van Leeuwen trophy for it, the very first edition.

q: By the end of 2017-18, which club had the best goal difference in an Eredivisie season, plus 90?
sub: They scored 112 and conceded 22 in 1997-98.
note: Duplicate. Same 1997-98 fact as two other rows in this slice, 112 goals scored and 89 points, and plus 90 is simply derived from them. Figure verified on the season page.

q: In which season did Ajax collect 89 points, the most in an Eredivisie season under three points for a win up to 2017-18?
note: Confirmed: 89 points in 1997-98, still the three-point-era high at the end of 2017-18.

q: Which club did Ajax beat 8-1 away in 1997-98?
note: Confirmed: De Graafschap 1-8 Ajax in 1997-98.

q: NAC's Koos Waslander scored after 8 seconds in March 1982. Which club were the opponents?
note: Confirmed: 8 seconds, 20 March 1982, NAC against PEC Zwolle. The record is now shared with Vito van Crooij from 2022, but naming Waslander keeps one answer.

q: Which PSV defender was sent off after 29 seconds at NAC Breda in 2014-15?
sub: The fastest red card the Eredivisie had seen.
note: 29 seconds confirmed on the records list. The sub claimed the KNVB threw the card out and he served no ban, which I could not confirm anywhere, so it is replaced.

q: Which Dutch referee took charge of 541 Eredivisie matches before retiring in 2010?
note: 541 matches confirmed, but his debut was 29 October 1983, NAC against VVV, so the date range was off by a season. Reworded to the retirement date.

q: Which Dutch referee was voted referee of the year for 2007-08 and then quit in July 2008 after a row with the KNVB?
note: Confirmed: referee of the year for 2007-08, then quit on 14 July 2008 after the KNVB told him he was no longer in the top ten.

q: Which Dutch referee, one of the first openly gay officials in the game, later ran refereeing at the KNVB?
note: Confirmed: one of the first openly gay referees in the game, and later head of refereeing for the professional game at the KNVB.

q: Which Dutch referee called on video assistants for the first time in an international, Italy against France in September 2016?
note: Confirmed: Italy against France, 1 September 2016, Kuipers called twice on Makkelie and Van Boekel.

q: FC Utrecht were playing in January 2017 when a referee in the Netherlands first used a pitchside monitor. Who were the opponents?
note: Confirmed: FC Utrecht against Cambuur, 25 January 2017.

q: In August 2018 a video referee ruled out an Eredivisie goal for the first time. Which club was denied?
sub: Fran Sol had punched it in, Maradona style, against VVV-Venlo.
note: Confirmed: 11 August 2018, Fran Sol's handball goal for Willem II at VVV-Venlo, ruled out by Kevin Blom.

q: Between 2009 and 2014, which four league positions played the Eredivisie play-offs for a European ticket?
note: Confirmed: positions five to eight from 2009 to 2014.

q: From 2015 the Eredivisie European play-offs were opened to which four league positions?
note: Confirmed: positions four to seven from 2015.

q: In which season did the Eredivisie bring back play-offs for European tickets, taking in the clubs from second to thirteenth?
note: Confirmed: the play-offs came back in 2005-06 for the clubs from second to thirteenth.

q: Which Alkmaar club won the Eredivisie in 1980-81 with six rounds still to play?
note: Confirmed: AZ '67 clinched it in round 28 of 34, so six rounds early.

q: Which Belgian striker was Eredivisie top scorer in 2010-11 with 23 goals for NEC?
note: Confirmed: 23 goals for NEC in 2010-11.

q: Which Breda club did Pierre van Hooijdonk score for in eleven league matches in a row in 1993-94?
note: Confirmed: eleven matches in a row for NAC in 1993-94.

q: Which club won the Eredivisie play-offs for a European ticket four times between 2010 and 2019?
note: Duplicate. Three of the four wins it aggregates already ship, Utrecht in 2010, 2013 and 2017 all appear in the shipping deck, and its own sub gives away the surviving 2019 row.

q: Which Ajax goalkeeper set an Eredivisie record in 1971 by going 1082 minutes without conceding?
note: 1082 minutes is his, but the records list dates it only to 1971 and his own page names no season, so the 1970-71 in the question was unsupported.

q: Which trophy for the least beaten goalkeeper in Dutch professional football did Voetbal International launch in 1972?
note: Confirmed: launched by Voetbal International in 1972 and first awarded for 1971-72.

q: Which Tilburg club lost fourteen league matches in a row between March and September 2010?
note: Confirmed: fourteen in a row, 20 March to 26 September 2010, equalling De Volewijckers of 1962-63.

q: Which Utrecht club won the first of the two Dutch play-offs for a UEFA Cup place, in 1987?
note: Confirmed: FC Utrecht won the 1987 play-off for the UEFA Cup place.

q: Which northern club won the 1988 Dutch play-off for a UEFA Cup place after finishing only eleventh in the league?
sub: UEFA refused to let the winner in again, so the KNVB scrapped it.
note: Confirmed: FC Groningen won it in 1988 from eleventh, and UEFA then refused the winner entry, which killed the format.

q: Which club were the first winners of the Dutch promotion play-offs, in 1973?
sub: A young Guus Hiddink was in that side.
note: Confirmed: De Graafschap won the first promotion play-off in 1972-73, with Hiddink in the side.

q: Which club scored only 16 goals in the whole of 1971-72, the fewest in an Eredivisie season up to 2017-18?
note: Confirmed: 16 goals in the whole of 1971-72.

q: Which club won just one of its 34 matches in 1970-71?
note: Confirmed: 1 win, 12 draws, 21 defeats, 14 points, bottom of 1970-71.

q: Which Dutch goalkeeper won the least beaten keeper trophy with PSV in both 1985-86 and 1986-87?
note: Confirmed on the trophy list, Van Breukelen for 1985-86 and 1986-87.

q: Which Rotterdam club did the goalkeeper Ed de Goey play for before joining Feyenoord in 1990?
note: Sparta is right but the number is not safe: the article prose says six seasons while its own infobox says 1985-1990. Took the count out.

q: How many points did Ajax take in 1971-72, the most in any Eredivisie season under two points for a win?
note: Confirmed: 63 points in 1971-72, the two-point-era record.

q: Which PSV defender was named Player of the Year at the first Eredivisie Awards, for 2017-18?
note: Confirmed: Arias was Player of the Year at the first Eredivisie Awards, for 2017-18. Worth knowing the shipping deck has Ziyech as Dutch Footballer of the Year for the same season. Different award, and 'PSV defender' keeps this one unambiguous.

q: Which Ajax winger was named Talent of the Year at the first Eredivisie Awards, for 2017-18?
note: Confirmed: Neres won Talent of the Year at the first Eredivisie Awards. Same caution as the Arias row, since shipping has De Ligt as Dutch Talent of the Year for 2017-18. 'Ajax winger' rules De Ligt out, so the answer stays single.

q: Which Dutch referee had been a serving police officer in Rotterdam alongside his refereeing career?
note: Confirmed: police officer and later inspector in Rotterdam.

q: Which club was relegated from the Eredivisie in 1959-60 with 29 points, the biggest haul by a relegated club up to 2017-18?
note: 29 points for Blauw-Wit in 1959-60 confirmed. Anchored the superlative to a closed season.

q: Which club conceded 111 goals in 1958-59, the most in any Eredivisie season up to 2017-18?
a: Holland Sport, the club known as SHS
note: 111 conceded by SHS in 1958-59 confirmed. Anchored the superlative.

q: Which Dutch referee made his Eredivisie debut in 2009-10 aged 24, the youngest debutant the league had had?
note: Confirmed: youngest Eredivisie debut, aged 24, in 2009-10. Reworded so it is a record set at the time rather than a standing one.

q: Which two clubs did Björn Kuipers referee in his last match, the 2021 Johan Cruijff Schaal?
note: Confirmed: his last match was the Johan Cruijff Schaal between Ajax and PSV on 7 August 2021.

q: Which Dutch referee lost a Champions League final and Euro 2000 to six months out with throat cancer in 1999?
note: Confirmed: six months out in 1999 with throat cancer, costing him a Champions League final and Euro 2000.

q: Which club did PSV beat 8-1 in October 1989 in a match that brought three own goals from the losers?
note: Duplicate. Same match and same answer as the ball row 'Which club scored three own goals in one match at PSV in October 1989'. Kept the ball one, the own goals are the story. Verified: PSV 8-1 MVV, 14 October 1989.

q: Which Ajax teenager scored on his Eredivisie debut in 2013-14, aged 17 years and 104 days?
note: Two problems: Riedewald is a defender, not a forward, and 'youngest player ever' is a live record. The exact age, 17 years and 104 days, is now in the question.

q: How many hat-tricks did Afonso Alves score in Heerenveen's 9-0 win over Heracles Almelo in October 2007?
note: Two defensible answers. nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_Alves describes one hat-trick inside 18 minutes and then four more goals in nine, not two hat-tricks. Seven goals can be counted either way, so a reader cannot judge it in a second.

q: Which Heerenveen team-mate scored the other two goals in the 9-0 win over Heracles Almelo in October 2007?
note: Confirmed: Gerald Sibon scored the other two in the 9-0.

q: Which coach took Afonso Alves off near the end of the 9-0 against Heracles so he could be applauded?
sub: Heerenveen finished with ten men because all three subs were used.
note: Confirmed: Verbeek took him off for the ovation, and Heerenveen finished with ten because all three substitutions were gone.

q: Which club took four penalties in one Eredivisie match against RBC Roosendaal in February 2005?
note: Confirmed: PSV took four penalties against RBC Roosendaal on 2 February 2005. Pulled from extreme to hard, with RBC named in the question PSV is a fair guess for a serious fan.

q: Which Ajax substitute was sent off 19 seconds after coming on in 1996-97?
note: Confirmed: sent off 19 seconds after coming on, 1996-97.

q: Which NEC defender collected 84 Eredivisie yellow cards, more than any other player up to 2017-18?
note: 84 yellows confirmed and the records list ties him to NEC, but he was a defender, not a midfielder. Also anchored the superlative.

q: Which ADO Den Haag defender scored three own goals in the 2014-15 Eredivisie season?
note: Confirmed: three own goals in 2014-15 for ADO. Baelum and Van Rhijn also managed three that season, but the ADO tag keeps this answer single.

q: Which defender put eight own goals past his own keepers in the Eredivisie for Feyenoord, Willem II and Heerenveen?
note: Confirmed: eight own goals, the Eredivisie record since 1 May 2021, across Feyenoord, Willem II and Heerenveen.

q: Which referee gave a penalty after 8 seconds in Heerenveen against Cambuur in 2014?
note: Penalty after 8 seconds, Heerenveen against Cambuur, Richard Liesveld, 2014, all confirmed. No source I could reach gives the month, so October is out.

q: Which Feyenoord midfielder was booked after 3 seconds against Ajax in 2008, equalling the Eredivisie record?
note: Confirmed: booked after 3 seconds against Ajax in 2008, equalling Kraay junior's 1992 mark.

q: Which Dordrecht '90 player was booked after 3 seconds at Feyenoord in 1992?
note: Kraay junior, 3 seconds, 1992, at Feyenoord, confirmed. Dropped the standing-record tail, since the record is now shared with Biseswar in 2008, who has his own row in this slice.

q: Which Rotterdam club went eleven matches and 1045 minutes without scoring across 1970-71 and 1971-72?
note: Confirmed: eleven matches and 1045 minutes without a goal across 1970-71 and 1971-72.

q: Which Eredivisie season averaged 3.88 goals a match, more than any other up to 2017-18?
note: 3.88 goals a match in 1958-59 confirmed. Anchored the superlative.

q: Which club went the whole of 1972-73 without drawing a single Eredivisie match?
note: Confirmed: Ajax drew none of their 34 in 1972-73. RKC did the same in 2009-10, so the season anchor is doing the work.

q: Which Rotterdam club drew eighteen of its 34 matches in 1974-75?
sub: PEC Zwolle in 1978-79 and FC Twente in 1988-89 later matched it.
note: Sparta's eighteen draws in 1974-75 confirmed. Took the standing-record claim out of the question and put the exact matching seasons in the sub.

q: Which club won its first seventeen matches of the 1987-88 Eredivisie?
note: Confirmed: seventeen straight wins from the start of 1987-88. PSV matched it in 2023-24, so the season anchor matters here.

q: Which club won nineteen Eredivisie matches in a row inside the 1971-72 season?
note: Confirmed: nineteen in a row inside 1971-72.

q: Which club fielded nineteen non-Dutch players at kick-off against FC Groningen in August 2010, an Eredivisie record?
note: Wrong and unsalvageable. The record reads 'Meeste niet-Nederlandse spelers aan de aftrap van een wedstrijd, 19, AZ tegen FC Groningen, 14 augustus 2010': nineteen across both starting elevens, not nineteen fielded by one club. No club can field nineteen players.

q: Which Brazilian was Eredivisie top scorer with PSV in 1994-95, aged just 18?
note: Ronaldo, PSV, 30 goals in 1994-95, aged 18, confirmed. 'The youngest Eredivisie top scorer' is a live record, so the age is stated instead of claimed.

q: Which 39-year-old scored an Eredivisie hat-trick for Sportclub Enschede in 1959-60?
note: 39 years and 163 days, Sportclub Enschede, 1959-60, confirmed. Removed the live 'oldest ever' framing, and dropped 'Frisian legend' because a shipping ball row already pairs that phrase with Sportclub Enschede and Abe Lenstra.

q: Which VVV forward scored an Eredivisie goal in 1961-62 aged 40 years and 255 days?
note: 40 years and 255 days in 1961-62 confirmed. Live record replaced by the exact age.

q: Which Volendam player scored an Eredivisie goal in 1959-60 aged 16 years and 100 days?
note: 16 years and 100 days in 1959-60 confirmed. Live record replaced by the exact age.

q: Which Iranian striker came off the bench on his PEC Zwolle debut in 2019 and scored four goals?
sub: It was 15 September 2019, against RKC Waalwijk.
note: Not his Eredivisie debut. He had already played two seasons for sc Heerenveen. It was his debut for PEC Zwolle, off the bench, on 15 September 2019 against RKC Waalwijk, and he scored four after coming on.

q: Dick Jol showed his 1000th Eredivisie yellow card in October 2007. A player of which club received it?
sub: The unlucky man was Civard Sprockel.
note: Confirmed: 20 October 2007, and the man booked was Civard Sprockel of Vitesse.

q: Which award did Dick Jol receive as Dutch referee of the year for 2007-08?
a: The Gouden Kaart, the Golden Card
note: Confirmed: the Gouden Kaart for 2007-08. Upgraded from the writer's 'likely' to confirmed.

q: Which two Dutch clubs did Dick Jol play for as a professional before he took up refereeing?
note: Confirmed: NEC and KV Kortrijk are the two professional clubs on his playing record.

q: Which Englishman replaced John Blankenstein as referee of the 1994 Champions League final days before the game?
note: Confirmed: Philip Don took the 1994 final. The reason was never made public, which the question wisely does not ask about.

q: Which Eredivisie club's coach did Roelof Luinge send to the stands twice for calling him names?
sub: The coach was Foppe de Haan.
note: Confirmed: Foppe de Haan of sc Heerenveen, sent to the stands twice for insulting him.

q: In which Eredivisie match did Roelof Luinge make his professional debut as a referee, in October 1983?
note: Confirmed: 29 October 1983, NAC against VVV.

q: Which Willem II midfielder had a yellow card upgraded to red by the first live video referee decision, in September 2016?
note: Duplicate by spoiler. It opens 'Which Willem II midfielder', which gives away the surviving normal row on the first live video decision. Dropped the extreme one because the deck is already heavy on extreme. Kali fact itself confirmed.

q: Which Dutch referee sat in a van outside the Philips Stadion as the first live video assistant, in a friendly in July 2016?
note: Confirmed: 26 July 2016 at the Philips Stadion, Makkelie in a van outside with the monitors while Ed Janssen refereed.

q: Which referee used the pitchside monitor for the first time in the Netherlands, in a cup tie in January 2017?
note: Confirmed: Van Boekel, FC Utrecht against Cambuur, 25 January 2017.

q: In a 2017 play-off between NAC and NEC a referee used video to take a red card back. Which NEC defender was reprieved?
note: Confirmed: Golla's red card withdrawn after review, NAC against NEC, 25 May 2017.

q: Which referee took a red card back after a video review in the NAC against NEC play-off of May 2017?
note: Confirmed: Dennis Higler was the referee who took the card back.

q: How many yellow cards did Björn Kuipers show in the 2014 Champions League final, a record for that match?
note: Confirmed: twelve yellows in the 2014 final, a record for that match.

q: Which club won the Eredivisie play-offs for a European ticket in 2019?
note: Confirmed on the play-off list, FC Utrecht won the European play-offs in 2019.

q: Which club won the second edition of the Dutch promotion play-offs, in 1974?
note: Confirmed: Wageningen won the second promotion play-off, in 1973-74.

q: From the 1981-82 season the Eredivisie changed its relegation. How many clubs went down directly from then?
sub: Until 1980-81 only two had gone down each season.
note: Duplicate. The shipping row 'Three clubs went down in 1981-82. Which two finished bottom with just 13 and 12 points' states this answer inside its own question.

q: How many clubs took part in the Eredivisie promotion and relegation play-offs each year between 2006 and 2019?
note: Confirmed: ten clubs a year from 2006 to 2019, the 16th and 17th from the Eredivisie plus eight from the first division.

q: Which PSV goalkeeper won the least beaten keeper trophy in 1977-78?
note: Confirmed on the trophy list, Van Beveren for 1977-78.

q: Which Feyenoord goalkeeper won the least beaten keeper trophy in 1978-79?
note: Confirmed on the trophy list, Treijtel for 1978-79.

q: Which Ajax goalkeeper won the least beaten keeper trophy in 1972-73?
note: Confirmed on the trophy list, Stuy for 1972-73.

q: Which Feyenoord goalkeeper won the least beaten keeper trophy in 1983-84?
note: Confirmed on the trophy list, Hiele for 1983-84.

q: Which club did the goalkeeper Nico van Zoghel score six of his seven Eredivisie goals for?
note: Duplicate. The surviving ball row's sub says 'Six of them came for Go Ahead', which is this entire question. Verified: seven in the Eredivisie, six for Go Ahead, two more in the second tier.

q: Who scored the Feyenoord goal against ADO Den Haag in September 2020 that won the first Eredivisie Goal of the Year?
sub: An overhead kick, voted the best goal of 2020-21.
note: Confirmed: Senesi's overhead kick against ADO Den Haag on 27 September 2020 won the first Goal of the Year, for 2020-21. Reworded so the answer is a name a reader can judge, not a description of a goal.

q: Which Heerenveen striker scored seven goals in one Eredivisie match in October 2007?
sub: It came in a 9-0 win over Heracles Almelo on 7 October 2007.
note: Seven goals on 7 October 2007 confirmed. The sub was a standing record in the present tense, replaced with the anchored detail.

q: Luis Suárez was banned for seven matches in 2010 for biting an opponent in Ajax against PSV. Who did he bite?
sub: The Dutch press christened him the Cannibal of Ajax.
note: Confirmed: November 2010, Ajax against PSV, Bakkal bitten on the shoulder, seven-match ban.

q: What did the Feyenoord goalkeeper Eddy Treijtel hit with a goal kick at Sparta in November 1970?
a: A seagull, which fell dead on the pitch
sub: Both clubs claim to have the stuffed bird in their museum.
note: Confirmed: 15 November 1970 at Sparta, the gull fell dead on the pitch, and both clubs claim the stuffed bird.

q: Which goalkeeper scored seven Eredivisie goals, more than any other keeper up to 2017-18?
sub: Six of them came for Go Ahead, and he added two in the second tier.
note: Seven in the Eredivisie plus two in the second tier confirmed on his page. Anchored the superlative.

q: The trophy for the least beaten keeper in Dutch football is named after a GVAV goalkeeper. What happened to him in June 1971?
a: He died in a car crash driving home from the KNVB ceremony
sub: Tonny van Leeuwen was 28.
note: Confirmed: 15 June 1971, a crash near Meppel at five in the morning on the way home from the KNVB ceremony, aged 28.

q: Which Ajax goalkeeper of the European Cup years was nicknamed Heinz Kroket for the way he fumbled high balls?
sub: Fans said he dropped them like a hot croquette.
note: Confirmed: Heinz Kroket, from the way he spilled high balls, the 1971 Wembley final being the notorious example.

q: Which goalkeeper answered to De Beer van de Meer, De Bolle van Zwolle and Het Lek van PEC?
note: Confirmed: all three nicknames, De Beer van de Meer at Ajax and the other two at PEC Zwolle.

q: Which Vitesse defender scored his first Eredivisie goal in 2017, after 303 matches without one?
sub: It came against Sparta Rotterdam on 10 March 2017.
note: Wrong club. The 303 goalless matches ran from 2002 to 2017 but the goal came for Vitesse, against Sparta Rotterdam on 10 March 2017. He was at Groningen from 2002 to 2008 and only returned later. The 25,000 minutes claim is unsourced, so it goes.

q: An FC Twente player set a grim Eredivisie record in 1987-88 by getting injured after how long?
sub: The unlucky man was Freddy ten Caat.
note: 15 seconds, Freddy ten Caat of FC Twente, 1987-88, confirmed on the records list. The cruciate ligament quote is unsourced, so the sub now just names him.

q: Which club scored three own goals in one match at PSV in October 1989?
sub: Hans Linders got two of them on his own.
note: Confirmed: 14 October 1989, PSV 8-1 MVV, Hans Linders two own goals and Coen Quaden the third.

q: Roelof Luinge's last professional match was a cup tie between Feyenoord and Ajax in May 2010. How did it end for him?
a: He was substituted in the 88th minute so the crowd could applaud him
note: Confirmed: 6 May 2010, the Feyenoord against Ajax cup final, replaced in the 88th minute by fourth official Kevin Blom so the crowd could applaud him.

q: Ajax won 12-1 at home to Vitesse in 1972 and 13-0 away in October 2020. Which club shipped the 13-0?
sub: It finished 0-13 in Venlo.
note: Both scorelines check out, 12-1 against Vitesse in 1972 and 0-13 at VVV-Venlo in 2020, but the question was a standing double record with a gimme answer. Recast onto the 13-0, which is the part that makes the table gasp.

q: Johan Cruyff, Johan Neeskens and Dick van Dijk all did the same thing in Ajax's 12-1 win over Vitesse in 1972. What?
sub: Cruyff actually took four, in Dick van Dijk's farewell match.
note: Confirmed, with a caveat now in the sub: Neeskens and Van Dijk got three each, Cruyff got four, Muhren and Hulshoff one apiece. The answer stands but the table deserves the detail.

q: Which day job did the Eredivisie referee Danny Makkelie combine with his whistle for years?
a: He was a police officer, later an inspector in Rotterdam
note: Duplicate. Exact mirror of the hard row 'Which Dutch referee had been a serving police officer in Rotterdam alongside his refereeing career'. Kept the hard one, since a ball answer that is only a job description makes nobody gasp.

q: Which Dutch keeper was still turning out in the Eredivisie for Go Ahead Eagles at the age of 44, in 1985?
sub: He was 44 years, 9 months and 14 days old.
note: 44 years, 9 months and 14 days in 1985 confirmed. The sub was a standing record, replaced with the exact age.
